LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 2.3.1 WORD CLASSES

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.3: Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Which things can you see and touch in the classroom?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify concrete and abstract nouns from a text
2. use concrete and abstract nouns correctly in a variety of contexts
3. appreciate the role of concrete and abstract nouns in communication

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: GRAMMAR IN USE 2.3.1 WORD CLASSES
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 6
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes helps you succeed in ENGLISH LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: GRAMMAR IN USE 2.3.1 WORD CLASSES
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify concrete and abstract nouns from a text

What this means
In this part you learn to identify concrete and abstract nouns from a text. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify concrete and abstract nouns from a text.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify concrete and abstract nouns from a text. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Use concrete and abstract nouns correctly in a variety of contexts

What this means
In this part you learn to use concrete and abstract nouns correctly in a variety of contexts. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use concrete and abstract nouns correctly in a variety of contexts.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use concrete and abstract nouns correctly in a variety of contexts. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate the role of concrete and abstract nouns in communication

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the role of concrete and abstract nouns in communication. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the role of concrete and abstract nouns in communication.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the role of concrete and abstract nouns in communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify concrete and abstract nouns from a text)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes to a partner. (skill: use concrete and abstract nouns correctly in a variety of contexts)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: appreciate the role of concrete and abstract nouns in communication)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify concrete and abstract nouns from a text.
3. Practise this skill: use concrete and abstract nouns correctly in a variety of contexts.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate the role of concrete and abstract nouns in communication.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 6 learner study Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Which things can you see and touch in the classroom?
2. Which things cannot be seen or touched?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Grammar in Use 2.3.1 Word Classes means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify concrete and abstract nouns from a text.
5. Be able to: use concrete and abstract nouns correctly in a variety of contexts.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
